title: DACHSER Live Transit Planner — sample journey dataset
purpose: End-to-end test journeys. Each one drives a single truck from origin to destination through the real API: plan, approve, depart, move along the road, meet simulated weather, re-plan, deliver.
honesty_note: Weather zones and vehicle positions in this dataset are SIMULATED and are labelled as such by the backend (source SIMULATION / MANUAL MAP SIMULATION). Road geometry, lanes, tariffs, holidays and driving bans come from the real providers and the real DACHSER CSVs.
timing_note: All times are relative to the moment the runner starts, so this dataset never goes stale.

journeys.title: Clear run — Karlsruhe to Nurnberg
journeys.what_it_proves: The happy path end to end: plan, approve, depart, move along real road geometry, arrive, record the actual outcome. No disruption.
journeys.expect: One approved route, steady progress to 100 percent, status DELIVERED, an actual-vs-planned outcome recorded.

journeys.title: Heavy snow on the A9 corridor forces a verified detour
journeys.what_it_proves: Live monitoring and automatic rerouting. The truck departs on a clear route; snow appears ahead near Hof; the system flags the approved route as impacted, finds a road-verified detour that clears the zone, the manager approves it, and the truck continues to delivery on the new road.
journeys.expect: After the zone is injected the current route becomes IMPACTED, a replan returns a CLEAR option, the decision is accepted, and the journey completes on the detour.

reference_point.where: A9 near Hof, sampled from captured OSRM geometry

weather_zones.note: Heavy snow band over the Thuringen / Hof stretch of the A9

journeys.title: 810k EUR shipment driving into the Sunday truck ban
journeys.what_it_proves: Pre-shipment risk plus the legal restriction engine. A high-value Saturday-evening departure with a Monday-morning deadline: the drive crosses into Sunday, so the planner must add the real ban waiting time rather than a flat penalty, score the risk, and warn before the shipment is scheduled.
journeys.expect: Legal waiting time visible in the ETA, an arrival pushed into Monday, risk MEDIUM or HIGH with stated reasons, and a deadline warning if the window cannot be met.

reference_point.where: A9 near Nurnberg, sampled from captured OSRM geometry

weather_zones.note: Persistent heavy rain around the Nurnberg interchange

journeys.title: Storm front across the corridor — detour or an honest hold
journeys.what_it_proves: The system never invents a way through. A severe storm front is laid across the whole Thuringen corridor as a line of overlapping zones. The planner must either verify a genuinely clear road around it — and show what that costs — or report that none exists and hold the vehicle.
journeys.expect: Either a wide, clearly costed detour, or NO_CLEAR_DETOUR with the journey held. Both are correct; what must never happen is a route drawn straight through the front.

weather_zones.note: Severe storm front across central Germany

journeys.title: Rain on the A7 — time against cost and fuel
journeys.what_it_proves: Complete-outcome optimisation rather than fastest-road optimisation. A moderate rain zone on a long north-south run produces a detour option that must be weighed on time, distance, fuel and cost before it is approved.
journeys.expect: A replan with at least one alternative, and a visible trade-off between the impacted route and the clear one.

weather_zones.note: Heavy rain band over the A7 around Kassel
